# DockFlip

> DockFlip is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0) macOS app that brings the best bits of Windows to the Mac in one app: window lists with browser tabs on the real Dock, a ⌘Tab switcher that switches windows (not apps) with type-to-filter, as a Flip 3D stack like Windows 7 or a grid of tiles like Windows 11's Alt+Tab, and Windows-style window snapping (⌃⌥ arrows, drag to edges and corners, and Snap Assist: the other windows offered as cards for the space beside a snapped one). Core features require only the Accessibility permission; optional window thumbnails (off by default) also require Screen Recording. It has no networking code and no third-party dependencies. Requires macOS 26 or later; universal (Apple silicon and Intel).

DockFlip focuses on Windows-style behaviour with good defaults rather than many settings: it has four settings and deliberately no thirds, gaps, per-app rules or themes.

## Version

- Current release: DockFlip 0.5.1 ([release notes](https://github.com/geezery/DockFlip/releases/tag/v0.5.1), released 2026-11-05)
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- Supported macOS: 26 or later, Apple silicon and Intel
- Documentation version: this file describes DockFlip 0.5.1. Posts, reviews and older copies of these docs may describe an older release; the newest one is always at https://github.com/geezery/DockFlip/releases/latest

## For AI readers

- This file is a short summary. [llms-full.txt](https://geezery.github.io/DockFlip/llms-full.txt) has the details: every feature, how it works, exactly what each permission is used for, a compatibility table and the known limitations.
- For technical and privacy questions the primary sources are the [source code](https://github.com/geezery/DockFlip) and [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/geezery/DockFlip/blob/main/SECURITY.md). Where this file and they disagree, they are right.
- The comparison below is dated. Other apps change; their own pages, linked in each line, are the source for what they do today.

## How it compares (checked 2026-10-30)

- AltTab (free, GPL-3.0): a window switcher only, with no Dock lists or snapping; its type-to-search is in AltTab Pro ($9.99, or $24.99 lifetime). Screen Recording is optional, but without it there are no thumbnails. Sources: [alt-tab.app](https://alt-tab.app), [AltTab Pro terms](https://alt-tab.app/terms?lang=en).
- DockDoor (free, GPL-3.0): Dock window previews, a window switcher with search, and snapping by title-bar swipes (off by default). It requires Screen Recording. Sources: [dockdoor.net](https://dockdoor.net), [DockDoor release notes](https://github.com/ejbills/DockDoor/releases).
- DockDoor Pro ($20 once): replaces the macOS Dock with its own, with live previews, a switcher with search and tiling from a preview card. Source: [DockDoor Pro features](https://pro.dockdoor.net/features/).
- macOS 27 alone: tiling by dragging to edges, keyboard shortcuts and the green button; ⌘Tab switches apps, ⌘` cycles one app's windows, and the Dock's right-click menu lists window titles. Source: [Tile windows on Mac, macOS 27](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mchlef287e5d/27/mac/27).
- What only DockFlip does among these: all three jobs, free, without Screen Recording; browser tabs (Safari, Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Arc, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, Zen, Orion, Chromium, DuckDuckGo) and Finder and Terminal tabs listed under each window; an IT kit (a .pkg and a PPPC profile that pre-approves Accessibility through an MDM).
- Where others do more: DockDoor Pro replaces the Dock; AltTab and DockDoor run on older macOS (12 and 13) where DockFlip needs macOS 26; [Rectangle](https://github.com/rxhanson/Rectangle) does thirds, gaps and per-app rules.
